article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Cartoq.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

raw_title: TVS’ Norton Atlas Adv For India – Top 10 Highlights You Should Know
title: Inside Look: TVS' Norton Atlas Adv For India - What Every Indian Car Owner Must Know
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - TVS Norton Atlas adv could debut in India in early 2027 as the Hosur-built adventure motorcycle gets a 585 cc twin and six-axis IMU rider aids Norton has begun deliveries of the Atlas adventure motorcycle in parts of Europe and we expect it to arrive in India in the early parts of next year. It has got the motorcycling community excited already and it will be interesting to see how the range gets priced in India. But before that, here are the top ten highlights: 1. Production at the Hosur plant Norton developed the Atlas at its Solihull headquarters but assembly takes place in Hosur, Tamil Nadu. The first examples rolled off the line on June 24, 2026. TVS has identified its Paddock retail concept for Norton motorcycles in India but a definitive launch schedule has not been established yet. 2. New 585 cc parallel-twin engine The liquid-cooled, DOHC parallel twin has a 270-degree crankshaft and develops 70 PS at 9,300 rpm. Peak torque stands at 57.5 Nm at 7,300 rpm. Its bore and stroke measure 78 mm and 61.2 mm. Atmospheric plasma-sprayed cylinder surfaces and twin oil pumps are other technical provisions. 3. Bosch six-axis IMU electronics The Bosch six-axis IMU supports lean-sensitive ABS and traction control in addition to wheelie, rear-lift and slide control. Cornering cruise control is standard as well. Riders can select five factory modes for varied road and traction conditions as they vary from wet-weather travel to off-road routes. 4. Atlas, Atlas GT and Apex variants The standard Atlas favours gravel roads and mixed-surface journeys. The Atlas GT, meanwhile, caters primarily to paved-road tours and has revised steering geometry, a lower seat and a different wheel configuration. Norton also lists an Atlas Apex version for customers who prefer additional electronic and convenience equipment. 5. Fully adjustable KYB suspension The standard Atlas receives a fully adjustable 43 mm upside-down KYB fork and a rear monoshock. Wheel travel stands at 180 mm at each end and the rear unit has hydraulic preload adjustment. By contrast, the road-biased GT has 140 mm travel at both ends. 6. Six-speed gearbox and quickshifter The six-speed transmission receives a bidirectional quickshifter as standard and thus easy clutchless upshifts and downshifts are possible. An assist-and-slipper wet clutch complements the electronic throttle. Power goes to the rear wheel via a chain and the twin-cylinder engine leads into an upswept 2-into-1 exhaust. 7. Wheels and adventure dimensions The Atlas runs on 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wheels and Norton lists cast-alloy and wire-spoke alternatives. Eurogrip Explo R Plus tyres measure 110/80 ZR19 at the front and 150/70 ZR17 at the rear. The seat is 845 mm high and ground clearance stands at 220 mm. 8. Steel trellis chassis and weight Norton has selected a steel trellis frame and the engine serves as a structural member. The rear swingarm is cast aluminium. The standard Atlas weighs 188 kg and the Apex 192 kg – measured before fuel is put into the tank. Fuel capacity stands at 15.4 litres and the wheelbase measures 1,465 mm. 9. Twin-disc front brake setup Twin 310 mm semi-floating front discs and radially mounted Bybre calipers handle the front brake accompanied by a 270 mm rear disc. raw_title: Vision S To Be One Of Mahindra’s Highlighting SUV Launches In 2027 – Here’s Why
title: Vision S To Be One Of Mahindra's Highlighting SUV Launches In 2027 - Here's Why
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Mahindra Vision S could debut in 2027 as a sub-four-metre SUV on the NU_IQ platform and offer a distinct alternative to the popular XUV 3XO Mahindra has an opportunity to put some of the character of its larger SUVs into a vehicle shorter than four metres. The Vision S concept offers a glimpse of how the company intends to do it. Its upright proportions and tailgate-mounted spare wheel set it apart from the XUV 3XO and could make it an attractive alternative for motorists who admire the Scorpio N but prefer a smaller vehicle. Commercially, the project assumes greater importance in light of Mahindra’s November 5 investor presentation. The company has earmarked June 2027 as the deadline for five product introductions, one of which will be an SUV on the NU_IQ platform. The Vision S is expected to be that vehicle and Mahindra plans to raise monthly NU_IQ production capacity at Chakan by 10,000 units by March 2028. Despite its modest exterior dimensions, the Vision S concept has a wheelbase of 2,665 mm. For perspective, the XUV 3XO measures 2,600 mm between its axles. Mahindra has also devised a flat floor for NU_IQ vehicles irrespective of the propulsion system. The extra space between the axles and the absence of a large central tunnel could prove especially useful for rear occupants. The NU_IQ gives Mahindra considerable freedom in its choice of engines. Petrol and diesel versions are possible alongside hybrid and electric derivatives while the architecture can accommodate either front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive. The 1.2-litre turbo petrol and 1.5-litre diesel units from the XUV 3XO are possible candidates for the initial models. How much of the concept will survive the transition to production? The test vehicles spied so far retain the boxy proportions, a prominent bonnet and a spare wheel on the side-hinged tailgate. The concept used cameras in place of exterior mirrors but the prototype has traditional mirrors. Flush door handles and a panoramic sunroof have also been evident. Stepping on the inside, the prototype departs somewhat from the show car. Earlier spy photographs revealed a multimedia screen set into the dashboard and physical controls below it. The concept had separate displays for the driver and infotainment functions and its cabin featured substantial grab handles for rear passengers. Mahindra originally presented the Vision S alongside the Vision T, Vision SXT and Vision X in August 2025. All four share NU_IQ and the architecture supports both right-hand-drive and left-hand-drive configurations. The Vision S could thus serve as the first real test of a vehicle platform that Mahindra intends to use internationally.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

title: 10 New Advs & Scramblers To Watch Out For - RE, Hero, Bajaj, Honda
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Here is a compilation of new adventure bikes and scramblers from Royal Enfield, Norton, Hero, Bajaj, Honda, Kawasaki and Brixton that could reach India in 2027 The choice of adventure motorcycles in India could look considerably different in 2027. Bajaj has a quarter-litre Adv on test and Norton could soon enter the market courtesy of TVS. Hero has explored two distinct interpretations of the Xpulse while Kawasaki has plans for both the trails and the highway. Even those who prefer an electric scrambler could have something to look forward to from Royal Enfield’s Flying Flea division. 1. Norton Atlas Norton could introduce the Atlas in India as early as January 2027 after photographs of another test motorcycle surfaced this week. TVS manufactures the 585 cc twin cylinder motorcycle locally at Hosur and the engine develops 69 bhp at 9,300 rpm and 57.5 Nm. Riders who spend more time on tarmac may prefer the Atlas GT as it has a 17-inch front wheel instead of the standard model’s 19-inch unit. 2. Bajaj Trekker 250 render Bajaj’s quarter-litre Adv has a familiar detail: the digital console seen on a test mule in October closely resembles that of the revised Pulsar N250. The latter’s 249.07 cc engine produces 24.5 PS and 21.5 Nm and could serve the new motorcycle too. The prototype also sports wire-spoked wheels and disc brakes at both ends. If the rumoured Trekker reaches showrooms in early 2027, the Xpulse 210 will have a direct rival from Bajaj. 3. Brixton Crossfire 500 Storr The Crossfire 500 Storr was originally due earlier this year but a display unit finally reached a dealership in Kolhapur in October. Its arrival in showrooms could give riders access to a 486 cc twin cylinder Adv for an estimated Rs. 5.60 lakh (ex-showroom). The engine produces 47.6 PS and 43 Nm and the Storr’s upright ergonomics and tall windscreen should come in handy on extended trips. 4. Kawasaki KLE500 Kawasaki intends to introduce the KLE500 in India within the next few months. Its 21-inch front wheel immediately distinguishes it from the Versys family and the 451 cc parallel twin produces 45 PS and 42.6 Nm in European specification. Kawasaki also has a 2027 SE SmartRide variant overseas. The centrifugal clutch on that version should make low speed manoeuvres easier on tricky trails. 5 & 6. Hero Xpulse 450 & Xpulse 150 Hero could have its own answer to the KLE500 by the second half of 2027. The Xpulse 450 made its debut in Milan earlier this month and its 421 cc liquid cooled single develops 46.6 PS and 38 Nm. Power reaches the rear wheel via a six-speed gearbox while the adjustable 43 mm KYB fork offers 225 mm of travel. The overseas debut could precede its arrival in India. Its smaller sibling, the Xpulse 150, is also a possibility. 7. Hero Xpulse Scrambler Hero has explored a slightly different interpretation of the Xpulse in scrambler guise. The trellis frame and engine casings on the concept suggest a relationship to the Xtreme 250R whose quarter-litre engine develops 30 bhp and 25 Nm. The 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wire-spoked wheels wear Pirelli Scorpion Rally STR tyres. Hero has yet to commit to series production. 8. Royal Enfield Flying Flea S6 The S6 takes the scrambler idea into electric territory. Royal Enfield’s Flying Flea division has earmarked summer 2027 for its second motorcycle and announced Dart Yellow and Lightning Grey as colour choices. Compared to the C6, the S6 has a larger front wheel and revisions to its seat and suspension. The battery capacity is still undisclosed. 9. Kawasaki Versys 900 Where the KLE500 caters to riders who venture off the tarmac, the Versys 900 could be a more attractive proposition for extended highway trips. It slots between the 650 and 1100 and uses a 948 cc inline four-cylinder engine rated at 122 PS and 97.3 Nm. Its electronic equipment comprises adaptive cruise control, forward collision warning and blind spot detection. Reports put its India debut in the first half of 2027. 10. Honda Africa Twin 1150 Honda unveiled three versions of the Africa Twin 1150 at EICMA and the motorcycle could return to India in 2027. The 1,131 cc parallel twin produces 119 PS and 119 Nm and can be paired to either a manual or dual-clutch transmission. Notably, Honda Sensing Ride is optional on the Adventure Sports. The company has yet to confirm a domestic launch.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_title: Festive 2026 EV Sales Get Past 5 Lakh Units For The 1st Time, Up 52.62%
title: Festive 2026 EV Sales Get Past 5 Lakh Units For The 1st Time, Up 52.62%
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Electric vehicle retail sales in India rose by 52.62 per cent in the 2026 festive season and two-wheelers made up nearly 65 per cent of the EV tally The record festive automobile retail tally in India this year owes much to electric vehicles. The Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA) recorded 5,09,667 EV registrations over 42 days between October 11 and November 21 as volumes rose 52.62 per cent from 3,33,935 units a year ago. It must be kept in mind that the net increase in EV registrations was greater than the increase in registrations of all vehicle types. The difference was 56,198 units and the rest of the reported market collectively shrank by that number. Electric vehicles represented 9.22 per cent of all festive registrations in 2026 compared to 6.18 per cent a year ago. Commercial vehicles exhibited the sharpest annual rise in percentage terms among the four EV categories. Electric CV registrations stood at 6,387 units as volumes rose 154.56 per cent from 2,509 units last year. Electric CVs represented 4.10 per cent of their respective vehicle segment compared to 1.73 per cent in 2025. Also Read: Electric Two-Wheeler Festive 2026 Sales Jump 61.10% To 3.31 Lakh Units S.No & Category (YoY) Festive 2026 Festive 2025 Festive 2024 1. Electric Two-Wheelers (61.10%) 3,30,846 2,05,373 1,99,209 2. Electric Three-Wheelers (25.45%) 1,20,330 95,920 88,745 3. Electric PVs (72.91%) 52,104 30,133 15,154 4. Electric CVs (154.56%) 6,387 2,509 1,089 Total (52.62%) 5,09,667 3,33,935 3,04,197 Electric two-wheelers were responsible for 71.40 per cent of the net increase in festive EV registrations. The category recorded 3,30,846 units as volumes rose 61.10 per cent from 2,05,373 units last year. The proportion of electric models in the overall two-wheeler market also increased to 7.67 per cent. Meanwhile, the three-wheeler category was the only one in which electric variants constituted a majority of registrations. Its electric share reached 62.16 per cent and 24,410 more electric three-wheelers were registered than in the 2025 festive season. The cumulative rise in electric passenger vehicle registrations since 2024 stood at 243.83 per cent. Also Read: EVs Outsell ICE-Powered Cars In Festive Season, Record 69% YoY Growth Its share of the EV market also increased from 4.98 per cent two years ago to 10.22 per cent this year. Electric passenger vehicles were the third largest of the four EV categories by volume. FADA compiled the nationwide registration figures on November 22 from 1,468 of the country’s 1,469 regional transport offices. The association did not have access to the 2026 festive registration data for commercial vehicles, three-wheelers and tractors in Telangana.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Dispatches and field testing reports from Cartoq.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

raw_title: New Toyota Innova Hycross vs Old: What’s Changed In The 2026 Facelift?
title: First Clear Look: Toyota Leaked With Major Design Upgrades Inside & Out
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Toyota’s popular three-row MPV gets a sharper front end, larger screens, a revised variant line-up and an updated strong-hybrid powertrain with E85 compatibility The Toyota Innova Hycross has received its first major update since its introduction in India in December 2022. The facelift isn’t a complete overhaul, and Toyota hasn’t changed the MPV’s overall proportions or its fundamental layout. The strong-hybrid version now gets a lithium-ion battery, higher combined power output and flex-fuel capability. Here’s what is different between the new and old models. 1. Exterior: A sharper face, familiar proportions The most noticeable changes are at the front. The new Innova Hycross gets a redesigned grille with a diamond-pattern mesh, replacing the honeycomb-style treatment on the outgoing model. The strong-hybrid variants also get new projector LED headlamps, with the LED DRLs integrated into the headlamp assembly. The fog lamps have been repositioned within sharper triangular housings, giving the front bumper a slightly more aggressive appearance. The rear gets subtle revisions as well. The tail-lamps retain their overall shape but feature updated internal lighting elements. The chrome strip connecting them has been replaced by a gloss-black finish, giving the tailgate a cleaner look. The 17-inch and 18-inch alloy wheel designs on the strong-hybrid variants also continue. The petrol GX gets 17-inch alloys, replacing the 16-inch wheels on the outgoing version. 2. Interior: Bigger screens make the biggest difference The cabin layout remains familiar, but the facelift brings a much-needed technology upgrade. The strong-hybrid VX and ZX variants now get a 12.3-inch touchscreen and a 12.3-inch fully digital instrument cluster. The outgoing model had a 10.1-inch infotainment screen and a 7-inch part-digital driver’s display. Toyota has also improved the equipment available on the mid-spec VX. It now gets a panoramic sunroof and wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity. The top-spec ZX continues with features such as powered second-row ottoman seats, ventilated front seats, an eight-way powered driver’s seat with memory, a nine-speaker JBL sound system and a powered tailgate. 3. Engine and hybrid technology: More power and E85 compatibility This is arguably the most important update. Both petrol and strong-hybrid versions continue to use a 2.0-litre, four-cylinder naturally aspirated petrol engine. The combined output of the strong-hybrid powertrain has increased from 184 hp to 197 hp. The electric motor continues to produce 206Nm, while the battery pack has been changed from the earlier nickel-metal hydride unit to a 56-cell lithium-ion battery. The updated strong-hybrid system can now run on ethanol blends ranging from E20 to E85, making it a significant development for Toyota’s electrification and alternative-fuel strategy in India. The petrol-only version continues to produce 173 hp, but its torque output has increased slightly from 205 Nm to 206 Nm. The strong-hybrid uses an e-CVT, while the petrol version continues with a CVT. 4. Safety and equipment: More technology across the range The overall safety package remains familiar, with six airbags, vehicle stability control, hill-start assist and an electronic parking brake with auto hold. The higher variants continue to get Toyota Safety Sense ADAS, a 360-degree camera and other convenience features. The ADAS package is now offered on the ZX, following the discontinuation of the earlier ZX (O) variant. The VX also gains equipment that was previously reserved for the VX (O), including a panoramic sunroof and wireless smartphone connectivity. 5. Price: The hybrid becomes more accessible The revised variant line-up has an interesting impact on pricing. Variant/powertrain Old Hycross New Hycross Petrol GX Rs 19.53 lakh Rs 19.59 lakh Petrol GX (O) Rs 20.97 lakh NA Strong hybrid entry-level Rs 26.76 lakh Rs 23.99 lakh Strong hybrid top-spec Rs 31.84 lakh Rs 31.99 lakh The new strong-hybrid GX brings the starting price down by Rs 2.77 lakh compared with the outgoing hybrid range. At the other end, the top-spec ZX is Rs 15,000 more expensive than the old ZX (O).

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. raw_title: New Gen Toyota Fortuner To Arrive Next Week – Top 5 Highlights
title: New Gen Toyota Fortuner To Arrive Next Week
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - New generation Toyota Fortuner could break the wraps on December 1 as substantial changes to its cabin, exterior and mechanicals are expected The Toyota Fortuner has gone more than eleven years without a generational change internationally and the development of its successor now seems to be close to completion. South African media reports have pointed to December 1, 2026 as the possible date of its world premiere. However, Toyota has not formally announced the schedule yet. Earlier this month, another camouflaged prototype surfaced in Argentina where the Fortuner goes by the SW4 moniker. Interestingly, Toyota introduced the ninth generation Hilux in India back in July at Rs. 31.99 lakh (ex-showroom). The mechanical relationship between the two vehicles offers some clues about the revisions in store for the seven-seater SUV. 1. New Interior & Features New Toyota Fortuner Rendering The cabin could benefit considerably from the technological advancements made to the Hilux this year. The pickup features a 12.3-inch infotainment screen, a 7-inch instrument display, wireless smartphone integration and an eight-speaker audio system. Expect similar equipment in the new Fortuner alongside a redesigned dashboard and centre console. The possible introduction of ADAS functions would also help Toyota address a notable omission in the existing SUV. 2. Diesel & Mild Hybrid Engines Toyota introduced 48 V mild hybrid technology to the Fortuner and Legender in India in June 2025 and its availability could extend to more variants upon the generational change. The existing 2.8-litre diesel develops 204 PS irrespective of the transmission choice. The peak torque output stands at 420 Nm for the six-speed manual version and 500 Nm for the automatic. The smaller 2.4-litre diesel could appeal to select overseas markets. 3. Extensive Exterior Changes Speculative Rendering Based On Spy Shots Judging by the test prototypes, Toyota has devoted much of its attention to the nose and tail of the SUV. The front fascia could receive angular headlamps, a reprofiled bonnet and a mesh grille. Meanwhile, the rear could sport a horizontal LED strip between the redesigned tail lamps. Relatively fewer changes are expected along the sides as the characteristic kink in the window line could survive. 4. Revised IMV Architecture Instead of switching to the TNGA-F architecture of the Land Cruiser 300, the Fortuner could utilise an evolved version of the existing IMV platform. The ladder frame construction will consequently be retained. Toyota could revise the suspension calibration and introduce electric power steering to improve manoeuvrability. Four-wheel drive variants are expected to retain a low-range transfer case and rear differential lock. 5. India Launch & Price Expectations The new Fortuner could reach India in 2027 where the existing model currently retails between Rs. 34.76 lakh and Rs. 50.46 lakh (ex-showroom). Toyota disclosed in October that cumulative domestic Fortuner sales had surpassed 3.3 lakh units. Its successor could command a higher asking price and face competition from the likes of the Skoda Kodiaq, Volkswagen Tayron and Jeep Meridian.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Dispatches and field testing reports from Cartoq.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

title: Royal Enfield Himalayan 750 Launched In India At Rs. 4.89 Lakh
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Royal Enfield Himalayan 750 debuts a 743 cc parallel twin engine and features adjustable Showa suspension, five ride modes and cruise control A decade after the original Himalayan 411 arrived, Royal Enfield has introduced a twin cylinder adventure motorcycle for the first time and it becomes its new flagship offering. The Himalayan 750 made its global debut at EICMA in Milan last month alongside the Continental GT 750. The dual-purpose adv has been launched in India at Rs. 4.89 lakh (ex-showroom). The new engine displaces 743 cc and develops 55 PS at 7,000 rpm. Peak torque arrives at 5,000 rpm but Royal Enfield specifies that 90 per cent of it is available at 3,500 rpm. In addition, the Himalayan uses a single overhead camshaft and retains the air and oil cooled configuration familiar from the brand’s 650 cc twins. Royal Enfield has devised a box section spine frame for the motorcycle and uses the engine as a structural member. The 750 has a standard seat height of 815 mm as opposed to 825 mm on the Himalayan 450. Its front wheel measures 19 inches instead of 21 inches and two brake discs take the place of the single disc on the smaller model. Specifications Himalayan 750 Engine Type Four-stroke parallel twin, SOHC Thermal System Air and oil cooled Displacement 743 cc Bore x Stroke 83.5 x 67.8 mm Compression Ratio 9.5:1 Maximum Power 55 PS at 7,000 rpm Maximum Torque 63 Nm at 5,000 rpm Idle Speed 1,300 rpm Clutch Wet multiplate Transmission Six-speed The suspension at either end comes from Showa. The 43 mm upside-down forks permit adjustments to preload, compression and rebound. The rear monoshock has a remote preload adjuster and a separate provision for rebound adjustment. The latter is useful when the rider needs to accommodate the extra weight of a pillion or luggage. Specifications Himalayan 750 Frame Box section steel spine Front Suspension 43 mm adjustable Showa USD forks Rear Suspension Showa monoshock and linkage Front Wheel Travel 190 mm Rear Wheel Travel 175 mm Front Brake Twin 280 mm discs Rear Brake 255 mm disc Calipers Two-piston at both ends Front Tyre 110/80 R19 Rear Tyre 150/70 R17 Wheel Options Cast alloy or tubeless spoked ABS Dual channel, switchable at rear Meanwhile, the Himalayan 750 offers five ride modes: Road, Road Sport, Rain, Trail, and Custom. The six-axis IMU enables lean-sensitive ABS and traction control. Riders can choose from three traction control levels or deactivate the function altogether. ABS can also be disengaged at the rear and each ride mode has its own throttle map and ABS parameters. Dimensions & Other Specs Himalayan 750 Overall Length 2,185 mm Overall Width 840 mm Overall Height 1,450 mm Wheelbase 1,522 mm Ground Clearance 205 mm Seat Height 815 mm Kerb Weight (90% Fuel and Oil) 224 kg Payload 194 kg Fuel Tank Capacity 17.8 litres Rake 27.9 degrees Trail 121.5 mm The circular TFT console measures four inches and supports navigation, music and telephone functions via smartphone connectivity. Royal Enfield also provides cruise control, a tyre pressure monitor and two USB Type-C ports of 27 W and 10 W respectively. The seven-inch headlamp uses LEDs and the turn indicators cancel automatically. The Wingman 2.0 system supports 4G connectivity and GPS. A total of five colour schemes has been presented by RE and they are Aztec Green, Tectonic Black, Siberia White, Viking Bronze and Antarctic Silver. The first two have alloy wheels while the other three sport wire spokes. Antarctic Silver also features Givi panniers and a top box, heated grips, hand guards and an aluminium sump guard.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

raw_title: New BMW M 1000 RR Launched In India At Rs. 59.90 Lakh, Gets 218 HP
title: New BMW M 1000 RR Launched In India At Rs. 59.90 Lakh, Gets 218 HP
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - BMW Motorrad’s flagship track-focused superbike gets more power, new M Winglets 3.0 and advanced slide-control technology BMW Motorrad has brought its latest M 1000 RR to India, giving its flagship superbike a significant performance and technology upgrade. Priced at Rs 59.90 lakh (ex-showroom), the new motorcycle arrives as a completely built-up unit (CBU), with bookings now open across BMW Motorrad dealerships. The M 1000 RR has always been about taking BMW’s superbike engineering as close to a race machine as possible while retaining road-going credentials. The latest version builds on that philosophy with a more powerful engine, revised aerodynamics and electronics designed to give experienced riders greater control when pushing the motorcycle on a racetrack. At the heart of the new M 1000 RR is a revised 999 cc, four-cylinder, liquid/oil-cooled engine. It now produces 218 hp at 14,500 rpm, an increase of 6hp over the previous model. Peak torque stands at 113 Nm at 11,100 rpm, while BMW claims a top speed of over 300 km/h. Also Read: Royal Enfield Posts Highest Ever Quarterly Bike Sales With 3.76 Lakh+ Units BMW has also introduced a shorter-throw throttle with a 58-degree rotation angle. This allows riders to access full throttle with less wrist movement, something that should be particularly useful when making quick inputs on a circuit. The engine is paired with a six-speed gearbox and gets a bi-directional Gear Shift Assistant Pro. One of the most noticeable changes is the redesigned front section. The new fairing is accompanied by M Winglets 3.0, made from carbon-fibre-reinforced plastic. These generate increased downforce, helping improve front-end stability and allowing riders to put more power down when accelerating out of corners. Also Read: 5 All-New Adventure Bikes Waiting To Launch From Indian Brands The electronics package gets two important additions. Dynamic Traction Control now incorporates Slide Control, which uses steering-angle sensor technology to help riders manage controlled acceleration drifts. The system effectively separates slip control and slide control, giving the rider more precise intervention depending on the situation. Unlike some markets where buyers may have to select additional equipment, the Indian-spec M 1000 RR gets the M Competition Package as standard. This includes M Carbon wheels, additional M Carbon components, a lighter M footrest system, an M Endurance chain and a milled and anodised swingarm pivot point. The package also includes activation for the M GPS Laptrigger. The motorcycle will be offered in a Blackstorm Metallic finish with M-colour graphics. It gets a 16.5-litre fuel tank, an 865 mm seat height and a claimed unladen weight of 194 kg. The technical specification sheet also lists a 120/70-section front tyre and a 200/55-section rear tyre, both mounted on 17-inch wheels. The new BMW M 1000 RR is priced at Rs 59.90 lakh (ex-showroom, India). It is available as a CBU import, and bookings have opened through the BMW Motorrad dealer network. BMW offers a three-year, unlimited-kilometre standard warranty, with an option to extend coverage into the fourth and fifth years. Roadside assistance is also included.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

title: Festive 2026: Tractor Sales Cross 1 Lakh Units As Mahindra Dominates
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Tractor festive sales passed 1 lakh units in 2026 as Mahindra and Swaraj secured 40.95 per cent of the separate October retail market Tractor registrations in India stood at 1,03,809 units during the 42-day festive season of 2026, against 1,01,532 units a year earlier. The increase of 2,277 units represented an annual improvement of 2.24 per cent. Sales crossed the 1 lakh threshold for the second consecutive festive season. The comparison against 2024 was more pronounced, as registrations then stood at 88,488 units, equivalent to a two-year increase of 17.31 per cent. Mahindra’s dominance is evident in the separate October 2026 manufacturer data published by FADA. The Mahindra tractor division registered 18,263 units for a 23.03 per cent market share, and the Swaraj division recorded 14,206 units or 17.92 per cent. Their combined 32,469 registrations represented 40.95 per cent of the 79,285 tractors sold in October. In October 2025, the same two divisions jointly held 39.46 per cent. International Tractors, the manufacturer of Sonalika, ranked third in October at 10,364 units and a 13.07 per cent share. TAFE occupied fourth position at 9,256 units and 11.67 per cent, ahead of Escorts Kubota at 8,331 units and 10.51 per cent. John Deere stood sixth, ahead of Eicher and CNH Industrial. The table below presents the complete October manufacturer figures separately from the festive category total. Tractor manufacturer (October only) Oct 2026 Oct 2025 Oct 2026 share Mahindra tractor division 18,263 16,967 23.03% Swaraj division 14,206 13,379 17.92% International Tractors (Sonalika) 10,364 9,151 13.07% TAFE 9,256 9,695 11.67% Escorts Kubota 8,331 7,902 10.51% John Deere 6,439 6,067 8.12% Eicher Tractors 4,858 4,729 6.13% CNH Industrial 3,992 3,096 5.04% Others 3,576 5,912 4.51% Total 79,285 76,898 100% The Mahindra 575 DI XP Plus and Swaraj 744 FE are established products in the two divisions’ tractor portfolios. In October 2026, Mahindra introduced Smart LIFT technology on the 575 DI XP Plus and 475 DI MS XP Plus. The FADA reports do not contain model-wise festive registrations, however, so the October manufacturer rankings cannot establish which individual tractor sold the greatest number of units over the 42-day season. Other relevant tractor models are the Sonalika DI 42 Sikander, Massey Ferguson 241 DI, John Deere 5050 D and Eicher 380. Among their manufacturers, Sonalika recorded an annual October increase of 13.26 per cent and CNH Industrial posted a 28.94 per cent rise. TAFE was an exception as its October registrations declined 4.53 per cent. The overall October tractor market improved 3.10 per cent from 76,898 to 79,285 units. Wheeled construction equipment recorded a different festive pattern from tractors. Registrations rose 26.06 per cent to 10,452 units from 8,291 a year earlier. Even after that recovery, the 2026 tally was 1.71 per cent below the 10,634 units registered in 2024. In the separate October construction equipment data, JCB ranked first at 3,942 units and a 53.03 per cent share. These figures refer to a different vehicle category and reporting period. The 2026 festive period ran from October 11 to November 21 compared to September 22 to November 2 in 2025 and October 3 to November 13 in 2024. Each interval comprised 42 days – from Navratri to 15 days after Dhanteras.

title: 2026 Festive Sales: Car Volumes Decline 7.16% To 7.48 Lakh Units
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Passenger vehicle retail sales fell by 7.16 per cent in the 2026 festive season in India but volumes were 16.43 per cent higher than two years ago The passenger car market recorded 7,48,616 units in the 2026 festive season as registrations fell 7.16 per cent from 8,06,322 units last year. On a daily basis, the average dropped from 19,198 units to 17,824 units. Passenger vehicles were the only category to post an annual decline in the festive report published by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA). The shortfall was considerably greater early in the season. Passenger vehicle registrations were down by over 18 per cent at Navratri according to FADA. The subsequent improvement around Dhanteras and Deepavali reduced the deficit and some festive bookings could result in registrations after the reporting period. As you might expect, Maruti Suzuki led the way with other popular brands Tata, Mahindra and Hyundai behind. It must be noted that electric cars and SUVs recorded a substantial increase in volumes even as the overall passenger vehicle market contracted. The non-electric segment recorded 6,96,512 units as volumes fell 10.27 per cent from 7,76,189 units a year ago. The electric segment partially offset that loss due to its good reception across different segments. Electric PVs (72.91%) 52,104 30,133 15,154 Total (-7.16%) 7,48,616 8,06,322 6,42,958 The contrast between the two propulsion categories becomes more pronounced over a two-year interval. The ICE passenger vehicle registrations were 10.94 per cent higher than in the festive season of 2024 while electric passenger vehicle registrations more than tripled. Electric models consequently represent a greater proportion of passenger vehicle registrations than they did two years ago. The implementation of GST 2.0 shortly before last year’s festive season resulted in an unusually high base for comparison. Total passenger vehicle registrations in 2026 were nevertheless higher by 1,05,658 units than in 2024. Meanwhile, the passenger vehicle share of nationwide festive registrations slipped from 14.92 per cent in 2025 to 13.55 per cent in 2026. Also Read: Mahindra To Launch Four New Models In The Coming Months Two-wheelers constituted the largest vehicle category in both periods and their annual increase in volumes outweighed the decline in passenger vehicle registrations. The 42 days in FADA’s festive study extend from the first day of Navratri to 15 days after Dhanteras to account for registration delays. The current period ran from October 11 to November 21 while last year’s figures were between September 22 and November 2.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Dispatches and field testing reports from Cartoq.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Punch, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. The brand has scheduled an event on December 3 to introduce JSW Motors and its first SUV, the Combat PHEV. Based on the Chery Jetour T2, the new model will bear the JSW badge. Its new website now accepts expressions of interest ahead of the presentation. Under the bonnet, the overseas Jetour T2 i-DM combines a 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engine and two electric motors via a three-speed dedicated hybrid transmission. An 18.4 kWh battery is expected for the Combat. Indeed, specifications differ between markets: Jetour quotes 224 PS and 390 Nm in Indonesia against 360 PS and 610 Nm in Malaysia. Jetour quotes 210 mm of ground clearance for the Indonesian T2 i-DM but specifications vary among overseas markets. The Jetour model has a 15.6-inch infotainment touchscreen and a 10.25-inch driver display. Level 2 driver assistance and an underbody-view camera system are also part of the international equipment list. JSW Motors plans local assembly at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra and a dealer network independent of MG outlets. The Combat is expected to enter the SUV market near alternatives such as the Skoda Kodiaq and Toyota Fortuner.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Cartoq.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

title: All-New Mahindra BE 07 Electric SUV Arriving Next Year
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Mahindra BE 07 electric SUV is expected in India by June 2027 and recent prototype sightings suggest the possibility of a seven-seater derivative Mahindra could soon have two electric SUVs that appeal to families in need of three rows of seats. The XEV 9S already serves that segment and photographs of a BE 07 prototype that surfaced on lately suggest the presence of a third row. Earlier spy images had revealed a five-seat interior and the possibility of two cabin layouts cannot be ruled out. The BE 07 will be the second model under Mahindra’s dedicated BE electric vehicle brand after the BE 6. The original concept debuted in August 2022 and Mahindra had initially planned to introduce its production counterpart in October 2026. The product roadmap disclosed in November now lists an unnamed electric SUV due by the end of June 2027. The BE 07 is expected to occupy that slot. The BE 07 concept had a wheelbase of 2,775 mm which was identical to that of the BE 05 concept. However, its overall length of 4,565 mm made it 195 mm longer. The exterior width and height stood at 1,900 mm and 1,660 mm respectively. Whether Mahindra has altered those dimensions for the production model is yet to be established. Spy Source: SearchEV/Instagram Battery options could mirror those of the BE 6 Sporteq since both SUVs share the INGLO platform. The smaller model currently offers three capacities of 59 kWh, 70 kWh and 79 kWh. Its rear axle motor develops up to 286 PS and 380 Nm while the largest battery provides an MIDC certified range of 708 km. The BE 07 could return a different range due to variations in weight and aerodynamics. Visually, the BE 07 has a more upright rear profile than the coupe styled BE 6. The prototypes have pronounced wheel arches and the tail lamps feature C-shaped illumination elements. The roof spoiler and extended rear section distinguish the silhouette. Mahindra has retained much of the angular design that characterised the original concept. On the inside, photographs of test vehicles have revealed provisions for three displays on the dashboard. The arrangement could resemble that of the XEV 9e and give the front passenger a screen of their own. Other anticipated features are a glass roof, a dashcam, multicolour ambient lights and Level 2 driver assistance technology. The homegrown brand’s original technical outline for INGLO specified lithium iron phosphate cells and DC charge rates of up to 175 kW. The architecture permits either rear-wheel drive or all-wheel drive. Whether the BE 07 will be available in a dual motor guise will depend on how Mahindra positions it relative to its other electric SUVs.
